SMTO-EXE-0108 — SMTO can't find the browser window it was using

GUID: aeacf2ca-e94f-5c1c-8d4f-1ce9e428e347
Slug: browser-session-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to keep working in a browser it opened earlier, but that browser is no longer running on the Gateway. Nothing was done in a browser by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO: "List the browser sessions you have open and continue in the right one." SMTO was holding an old reference; the list shows only browsers that are really running now.
  2. If the list is empty, ask SMTO to start a new browser session and go back to the page you need. Browsers SMTO opens end when they are closed or when the Gateway restarts, so a fresh one is needed.
  3. Check that you are still using the same Gateway as when the browser was opened. The selected Gateway is shown under the message box. Each browser belongs to one Gateway, so switching Gateways makes the old browser unreachable.
  4. If you had signed in to a website in the old browser, sign in again in the new one. A new temporary browser starts without the sign-ins from the old one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO continues the task in a browser that appears in its list, and the expected web page loads.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, mentioning whether the Gateway was restarted. Don't paste passwords or saved browser data into the chat to recreate a sign-in.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's browser service has no session with the supplied browser_session_id (it was stopped, the Gateway restarted, or the ID came from another Gateway).

What this means

  • The supplied browser session ID was absent from the backend's current session map. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The supplied browser session ID was absent from the backend's current session map.

How to diagnose it

  • List sessions on the same Gateway and inspect whether the original session ended or the ID belongs to another service lifetime.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._session found no entry for browser_session_id in the Gateway's in-memory session map; sessions end on stop/detach and do not survive a Gateway restart. Call browser.sessions on the same selected Gateway and use a returned browser_session_id, or browser.start a new managed session; never reuse IDs from before a restart.
  • Use browser.sessions and select a returned session ID, or start a new managed session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use browser.sessions and select a returned session ID, or start a new managed session.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended current session ID resolves under the owning conversation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
